subject: general
question: The average of ten numbers is 7. If each number is multiplied by 12, then the average of the new set of numbers will be:
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
If every number in a set is **multiplied** by a constant **k**, the **new average** is also multiplied by **k**.

Original Average = 7

Multiplier (k) = 12

New Average = 7 × 12 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

**__Alternate Method__**
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/465a8d87fa6d5c95d59f63e316cdb737789b54bd3cd925fec77b98761d35513d.png] 
**Given:**

Number of terms (n) = 10

Original Average = 7

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of 10 numbers = 10 × 7 = 70

⇒ Each number is multiplied by 12, so the new sum = 70 × 12

⇒ New Sum = 840

⇒ New Average = New Sum ÷ 10

⇒ New Average = 840 ÷ 10 = 84

**∴ The correct answer is 84.**

**__Additional Information__**

Effect of Addition/Subtraction

If a constant **a** is added to or subtracted from every term, the new average becomes **Original Average ± a**.

Effect of Division

If every term is divided by a non-zero constant **k**, the new average becomes **Original Average ÷ k**.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, Weighted Avg = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p
